newsitem.title: GERMANY: Dresdner sees strong Q4 trading income.
newsitem.headline: Dresdner sees strong Q4 trading income.

text.p: Germany's Dresdner Bank AG is confident of achieving strong trading income in the last quarter of 1996 although income dropped in the first nine months, a spokesman said on Thursday.
Dresdner's fourth quarter trading income will be "certainly around 200 million marks ($132.3 million) ," a spokesman told Reuters.

Earlier the bank said its nine month trading income dropped 14.8 percent to 456.2 million marks but said it would post a double digit rise in income for the full year once pending earnings were realised.
But the bank's trading income dropped 14.8 percent to 456.2 million marks in the period, as Dresdner said it was still waiting to realise pending earnings.
Year-end trading income should show a double-digit rise, the bank said, and a spokesman later added that the bank was confident of earning 200 million marks in its own account in the final quarter.
The Dresdner spokesman also said the bank's full year operating profit would rise by more than 10 or 15 percent.
Net commission income rose 42 percent to 2.8 billion marks, largely boosted by the integration of Dresdner's merchant banking unit Kleinwort Benson.
Administrative costs rose to 6.09 billion marks from 5.15 billion marks but not counting the Kleinwort integration, the increase would have been 4.9 percent, Dresdner said.
The bank also made a long expected announcement that it would launch a direct banking unit, following a path already taken by its major rivals in Germany.
Dresdner said the direct bank would get off the ground in the second half of 1997 but did not give any details, other than to say the unit would be innovatively structured.
